tamp — small-core, plugin-driven build automation framework

USAGE:
  dotnet tamp init [--solution <path>] [--dry-run]    scaffold Build.cs into the current dir
  dotnet tamp mcp                                     start the MCP control-surface server (stdio)
  dotnet tamp migrate nuke [--dry-run] [...]          convert a NUKE build to Tamp (preview; runs Tamp.Migrate)
  dotnet tamp <target> [--dry-run | --plan | --list | --list-tree] [--<param> <value>]
  dotnet tamp --version | --help

INSTALL:
  dotnet tool install --global Tamp.Cli            (or --local, with a tool manifest)

FLAGS:
  --dry-run            Print every CommandPlan that would run; execute nothing.
  --plan               Render the target dependency graph; execute nothing.
  --list               List top-level targets (or all, if none are marked).
  --list-tree          List targets with their dependencies.
  --all                Used with --list / --list-tree: show internal targets too.
  --verbosity <level>  quiet | minimal | normal | verbose | diagnostic
  --quiet | -v         Shortcuts for --verbosity quiet | --verbosity verbose

Tamp locates a build project under build/, _build/, or .tamp/build/ in the
current working tree (or an ancestor) and forwards the invocation to it.

Documentation: https://github.com/tamp-build/tamp

tamp init — scaffold a Tamp build script into the current directory

USAGE:
  tamp init [--template <name>] [--solution <path>] [--tamp-version <x>] [--dry-run] [--force] [--list-templates]

TEMPLATES (embedded — offline-safe):
  minimal     Clean / Restore / Compile / Test (default)
  library     minimal + typed Pack target with nupkg output dir
  monorepo    per-project Test fan-out + Ci aggregate + Pack

WHAT IT WRITES (any template):
  build/Build.cs               build script (shape varies by template)
  build/Build.csproj           pins Tamp.Core + Tamp.NetCli.V10
  (all Tamp pins use one version: the newest stable Tamp.Core on NuGet, never older
   than this CLI; this CLI's own version if NuGet can't be reached within 5s)
  .config/dotnet-tools.json    registers dotnet-tamp as a local tool (if absent)
  tamp.sh + tamp.cmd           shims that `dotnet tool restore` on first run

FLAGS:
  --template <name>          Pick a non-minimal template (minimal | library | monorepo)
  --settings-style <style>   Wrapper settings shape in scaffolded Build.cs (fluent | init).
                              fluent (default) → DotNet.Build(s => s.SetProject(...))
                              init             → DotNet.Build(new() { Project = ... })
  --solution <path>          Explicit .NET solution path (otherwise auto-detected)
  --tamp-version <x>         Pin this Tamp version (Tamp.Core, Tamp.NetCli.V10, dotnet-tamp);
                              skips the NuGet lookup
  --dry-run                  Print would-write list; touch nothing
  --force                    Overwrite existing files
  --list-templates           List templates from all registered sources
  -h | --help                This message

RESERVED (parsed; not implemented):
  --template-source <pkg>    (0.3.0)  Pin a specific NuGet template package
  --offline                  (0.3.0)  Refuse network fallback
  --with-ci <vendor>         (0.3.0)  Emit CI workflow files
  --interactive              (0.4.0)  Prompt for choices

ENVIRONMENT:
  TAMP_INIT_FEED_U
[truncated]

Description:
  Executes a tool from source without permanently installing it.

Usage:
  dotnet tool execute <packageId> [<commandArguments>...] [options]

Arguments:
  <packageId>         Package reference in the form of a package identifier 
                      like 'dotnetsay' or package identifier and version 
                      separated by '@' like 'dotnetsay@2.1.7'.
  <commandArguments>  Arguments forwarded to the tool

Options:
  --version <VERSION>       The version of the tool package to install.
  --allow-roll-forward      Allow a .NET tool to roll forward to newer versions 
                            of the .NET runtime if the runtime it targets isn't 
                            installed. [default: False]
  --prerelease              Include pre-release packages. [default: False]
  --configfile <FILE>       The NuGet configuration file to use.
  --source <SOURCE>         Replace all NuGet package sources to use during 
                            installation with these.
  --add-source <ADDSOURCE>  Add an additional NuGet package source to use 
                            during installation.
  -v, --verbosity <LEVEL>   Set the MSBuild verbosity level. Allowed values are 
                            q[uiet], m[inimal], n[ormal], d[etailed], and 
                            diag[nostic]. [default: normal]
  --disable-parallel        Prevent restoring multiple projects in parallel. 
                            [default: False]
  --ignore-failed-sources   Treat package source failures as warnings. 
                            [default: False]
  --no-http-cache           Do not cache packages and http requests. [default: 
                            False]
  --interactive             Allows the command to stop and wait for user input 
                            or action (for example to complete authentication). 
                            [default: False]
  -?, -h, --help            Show command line help.
